recommendations.regimenLabel: Anticoagulation (DOAC or LMWH) on confirmed/high-probability PE
steps: Start anticoagulation on clinical suspicion if high probability (LMWH/DOAC).
Massive PE (shock): thrombolysis (or embolectomy) and resuscitation.
Confirm with CTPA (or V/Q); echo for RV strain in unstable patients.
Continue DOAC/LMWH→oral; duration ≥3 months (longer if unprovoked/recurrent).
Oxygen, analgesia; assess for cancer/thrombophilia if unprovoked.

drugRefs.dose: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily
drugRefs.why: First-line oral anticoagulation for haemodynamically stable PE; no parenteral lead-in required.

drugRefs.dose: 15 mg twice daily for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily
drugRefs.why: Alternative first-line DOAC; take the 15/20 mg maintenance dose with food.

drugRefs.dose: 1.5 mg/kg once daily (or 1 mg/kg every 12 hours)
drugRefs.why: Parenteral option when DOACs are unsuitable and as a lead-in for warfarin; preferred in active cancer and pregnancy.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism (Ch. 290)
ESC 2019 Guidelines on the Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism

recommendations.regimenLabel: Reperfusion / parenteral therapy for high-risk (massive) PE

drugRefs.why: For haemodynamically unstable (high-risk) PE; rapidly lyses clot. Surgical/catheter embolectomy if thrombolysis contraindicated or failed.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: IV unfractionated heparin (unstable / peri-thrombolysis / renal failure)
drugRefs.dose: 80 units/kg bolus, then 18 units/kg/hour infusion titrated to APTT
drugRefs.why: Preferred anticoagulant when thrombolysis is planned, in haemodynamic instability, or severe renal impairment, because of its short half-life and reversibility.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Deep Venous Thrombosis and Pulmonary Thromboembolism (Ch. 290)
ESC 2019 Guidelines on the Diagnosis and Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism

confirm: Pleuritic pain/dyspnoea/tachycardia ± leg DVT; risk-stratify (Wells), D-dimer if low probability, CTPA to confirm.
